fact_check_log.claim: Key takeaway 2: order certificates and apostilles early; DFAT publishes no set turnaround; Atto Notorio with four unrelated witnesses, not more than six months before
Melbourne books through Prenot@mi, the consulate's online booking portal; proof of address in Victoria or Tasmania
Living outside Australia: Embassy points to the Italian consulate in the state where you reside; Melbourne asks for VIC/TAS proof of address
Not published: whether an Italian consulate in another country issues the Atto Notorio to an Australian living there (no marker, correctly labelled not published)
Tribunale Civile: by appointment, two adult witnesses, interpreter if needed; neither spouse can act as witness or interpreter
Official Italian translation by a NAATI-certified translator, then notarisation, then apostilles on original and translation
Passport Office lodgement by appointment, where someone can attend on your behalf, or registered mail
Bagno a Ripoli does not provide an interpreter, so you bring your own
Timeline notes: Bagno a Ripoli 90 days' notice; harder May to September; DFAT no set turnaround; Adelaide two weeks; Brisbane one month; Rome/Milan lead times not published
Some steps are yours alone: both of you attend the Atto Notorio (generalised from Sydney's rule)
Each Australian signs the Nulla Osta in person in Rome or Milan
Civil wedding: both partners foreign and non-resident, Bagno a Ripoli takes a sworn declaration instead of banns
Marry in Australia: legal wedding at home before an authorised celebrant and two witnesses; Italy day is symbolic
Close: one Wedded Advisor, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, plans venue, travel, vendors and payments
Close: we contract and hold your suppliers; the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins; someone on the ground looks after the days that matter
Same-sex: Italy offers civil union, not marriage
